title: SignalFox — AI-Powered Conversational Intelligence for Enterprise Sales
content:
SignalFox is the AI platform that makes every sales rep your best sales rep. We analyze sales conversations in real time — calls, emails, meetings — and deliver live coaching, deal intelligence, and revenue insights that help enterprise sales teams close more deals, faster.

Today's sales intelligence tools tell you what happened after the call is over. SignalFox tells you what to do while the conversation is still happening. Our real-time coaching engine analyzes live sales conversations and surfaces relevant talking points, competitive responses, and objection-handling strategies directly to the rep during the call.

Beyond real-time coaching, SignalFox provides comprehensive deal intelligence: automatic conversation summaries, risk scoring for every opportunity, multi-threaded relationship mapping, and predictive forecasting based on actual conversation signals rather than self-reported CRM data.

Founded in 2023 by Amira Hassan, former VP of AI Products at Salesforce, and Jake Williams, formerly of OpenAI's applied AI team, SignalFox combines deep enterprise sales expertise with cutting-edge AI. Amira spent a decade building AI products for the world's largest sales platform. Jake helped build the AI models that power a new generation of intelligent applications.

Based in New York, our team of 30 serves 42 enterprise customers with a net revenue retention rate of 145%. SignalFox integrates with your existing sales stack — Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Slack — and delivers value from day one.

title: SignalFox — First Meeting with Amira Hassan (CEO)

content:

Current tools like Gong and Chorus analyze conversations after the fact — useful for coaching and forecasting, but they miss the opportunity to help reps in the moment. Sales managers can't sit in on every call.

- **Solution**: SignalFox provides real-time conversational intelligence. During a live sales call, the platform analyzes the conversation and surfaces on-screen prompts: relevant case studies when a competitor is mentioned, objection-handling strategies when pricing pushback occurs, technical specs when the prospect asks about integrations. Post-call, it provides deal scoring, conversation summaries, and predictive analytics.

- **Traction**: 42 enterprise customers. $2.8M ARR. 145% net revenue retention — this is exceptional. Growing 28% QoQ. Usage-based pricing means customers naturally expand as they have more sales conversations.

- **Team**: Amira Hassan (CEO) was VP of AI Products at Salesforce for 6 years — led the team that built Einstein for Sales. Jake Williams (CTO) was on OpenAI's applied team, building real-world AI applications. 30 employees, primarily in New York.

- **Fundraise**: Series A, targeting ~$14M. $4.5M seed from First Round Capital (2023).

I'm immediately excited about this one. The NRR of 145% is a standout metric — it tells me customers are getting real value and expanding usage aggressively. Amira is the right founder for this — she built AI sales tools at Salesforce and knows exactly where they fell short. The real-time coaching angle is a genuine product differentiator vs Gong. title: SignalFox — Product Demo and Technical Review with Jake Williams (CTO)
author: David Okonkwo
content:
Meeting: Product demo and technical deep-dive — SignalFox
Date: February 18, 2026
Attendees: David Okonkwo (AIVC), Jake Williams (CTO, SignalFox), Amira Hassan (CEO)
Location: SignalFox office, New York

## Summary

In-person demo of the full product. Saw the real-time coaching in action on a simulated sales call. Also went deep on the technical architecture with Jake. Very impressed.

## Product Demo

- **Real-Time Coaching**: Jake ran a simulated enterprise sales call while I watched the coaching interface. During the call:
  - When the "prospect" mentioned evaluating a competitor, a sidebar instantly surfaced competitive differentiators and a relevant case study
  - When pricing objections came up, the system suggested three response strategies with success rates based on historical data
  - When the conversation went off-track, a gentle nudge appeared to bring it back to the discovery agenda
  - After the call, a full summary appeared in 30 seconds with action items, sentiment analysis, and deal risk score

- **Deal Intelligence Dashboard**: Portfolio-level view of all active deals. Each opportunity has a health score based on actual conversation signals (not self-reported CRM data). Multi-threaded view shows which stakeholders have been engaged and which haven't. Predicted close dates are adjusted based on conversation momentum.

- **Integration**: Works with Zoom, Teams, Google Meet for video calls. Dialpad and Twilio for phone. Salesforce and HubSpot for CRM sync. Data flows in real-time — the moment a call starts, SignalFox is listening and analyzing.

## Technical Architecture

- Jake's OpenAI background shows in the model architecture. Custom LLM fine-tuned on millions of sales conversations. Real-time transcription + analysis pipeline runs in under 2 seconds (fast enough for live prompts).

- The competitive moat is in the training data: every conversation improves the model's understanding of what works in different sales scenarios. With 42 customers generating thousands of calls per week, they're building a flywheel.

- **Concern**: The real-time latency is impressive but Jake acknowledged it's compute-intensive. Current infrastructure costs are high. They're working on optimization but it could affect margins at scale.

## My Assessment

This is not just an incremental improvement over Gong — it's a category shift. Gong tells you what happened; SignalFox helps you in the moment. The product demo was the most compelling I've seen this year. The usage-based expansion motion is a beautiful business model for conversational AI.

title: SignalFox — Term Sheet Negotiation Update

Ongoing term sheet negotiation. Two main points of discussion: valuation and board structure.

- AIVC offered: $50M pre-money
- Amira countered: $60M pre-money
- Her argument: NRR of 145% is in the top decile of Series A companies. Revenue growth is accelerating. Comparable companies (Gong at Series A, Clari at Series A) were valued at higher multiples on weaker NRR.

- My view: $60M is too rich for $2.8M ARR. That's ~21x ARR, which is above market for conversational intelligence. I'm willing to go to $55M (19.6x) to acknowledge the exceptional NRR, but not higher. At $55M, $9M from AIVC gets us ~14% ownership, which is our target range.

## Board Structure

- Standard AIVC ask: 1 board seat (David Okonkwo), 2 founder seats, 1 independent
- Amira's ask: Reserve 2 additional board seats for future rounds
- This is unusual at Series A but I understand the logic — she wants to control board dynamics through Series B. I'm comfortable with this as long as the independent seat is agreed upon.

## Competitive Dynamics

- First Round Capital will follow on with $2M
- Remaining $3M being filled by angels and small funds
- No other lead investor competing with us — First Round introduced us specifically. This is a positive signal that Amira wants AIVC, which gives us some negotiating leverage.

## James's Valuation Analysis

- James pulled comp data: median Series A pre-money for conversational intelligence companies (2024-2026) is $42M. SignalFox's NRR (145%) is in the top 10%. Adjusting for NRR quality, $50-55M is defensible.

## Next Steps

- [ ] If she accepts, move to legal documentation immediately
- [ ] Target close by end of June

title: Market Research: Conversational Intelligence Landscape
author: Elena Rodriguez
content:
From: Elena Rodriguez
To: David Okonkwo
Date: March 10, 2026
Subject: SignalFox — Conversational Intelligence Market Research

David,

Here's my research on the conversational intelligence market. Bottom line: large market, clear category leader (Gong), but real-time coaching is a new sub-segment with no dominant player.

**Market Overview**:
- Global conversational intelligence market estimated at $3.4B in 2025, projected to reach $5.2B by 2028 (35% CAGR)
- Driven by: remote/hybrid sales teams generating more recorded conversations, AI capabilities improving dramatically, enterprise focus on sales productivity
- Primary buyer: VP of Sales / CRO. Budget comes from sales operations.

**Competitive Landscape**:

1. **Gong** ($7.5B valuation, Series E): Market leader. Dominant in call recording, analysis, and deal intelligence. 4,000+ customers. Recently raised $250M to build "enterprise AI platform." Strength: brand, installed base, data moat. Weakness: post-call analytics only — no real-time coaching. Culture is data analytics, not AI-native.

2. **Chorus (ZoomInfo)**: Acquired by ZoomInfo in 2021. Being integrated across ZoomInfo's revenue intelligence platform. Strength: bundled with ZoomInfo data. Weakness: losing standalone innovation as it gets absorbed.

3. **Clari**: Revenue intelligence platform. More focused on forecasting and pipeline management than conversational analysis. Different angle — not directly competitive with SignalFox's real-time coaching.

4. **Observe.ai**: Contact center conversational intelligence. Different market (customer support vs sales). Not directly competitive.

5. **Real-time coaching**: This is a NEW category. No clear leader. SignalFox appears to be the most advanced. Wingman (acquired by Clari) had early real-time features but the product stalled post-acquisition.

**Key Insight**: The shift from post-call analytics to real-time coaching mirrors the broader AI trend from "analytics" to "copilot." Just as GitHub Copilot transformed developer tools from analysis to real-time assistance, SignalFox is doing the same for sales. This is a category-defining opportunity.

**Risk**: Gong has the resources and data to build real-time coaching. If they prioritize it, they could launch within 12-18 months. But their platform architecture is built around post-call processing — retrofitting for real-time would require significant re-architecture.

Happy to discuss.

Elena

title: Real-Time AI Sales Coaching: The Next Frontier Beyond Call Recording
author: Jason Lemkin
content:
Real-Time AI Sales Coaching: The Next Frontier Beyond Call Recording
By Jason Lemkin | SaaStr | February 15, 2026

I've been saying for years that conversational intelligence would become table stakes for every B2B sales team. Gong proved the model. But now a new wave of startups is asking: what if we could coach reps in real-time, not just analyze their calls after the fact?

The company that caught my attention is SignalFox, a New York-based startup founded by Amira Hassan (ex-Salesforce VP of AI Products) and Jake Williams (ex-OpenAI). Their platform doesn't just record and transcribe sales calls — it provides live coaching prompts during the conversation.

I got a demo last month and I'll be honest: it's impressive. During a simulated sales call, SignalFox surfaced competitive intelligence when a rival was mentioned, suggested talk tracks when the prospect raised an objection, and even flagged when the rep was talking too much versus listening. All in real-time, with less than 2 seconds of latency.

"Post-call analysis is like watching game film," Hassan told me. "It's useful, but the game is already over. Real-time coaching is like having a coach in your ear during the actual play. That's where the value is."

The numbers back it up: 42 enterprise customers, $2.8M in ARR, and a net revenue retention rate of 145%. That NRR is Datadog territory for a company barely two years old. Customers expand because SignalFox charges based on usage — more reps, more calls, more revenue.

Of course, the elephant in the room is Gong. With a $7.5B valuation and 4,000+ customers, Gong has the resources and the data to build real-time coaching. Hassan's response: "Gong's architecture was built for post-call processing. Retrofitting for real-time is like adding a turbocharger to a diesel engine — possible but not optimal. We built for real-time from day one."

SignalFox is raising a Series A. If the NRR holds and they can fend off Gong, this could be one of the more interesting enterprise AI companies of the vintage.

title: Enterprise Sales Teams Increasingly Turn to AI for Deal Intelligence
author: Thomas Davenport
content:
Enterprise Sales Teams Increasingly Turn to AI for Deal Intelligence
By Thomas H. Davenport | Harvard Business Review | March 20, 2026

The enterprise sales function is undergoing its most significant technological transformation since the adoption of CRM systems two decades ago. AI-powered tools for conversational intelligence, deal forecasting, and sales coaching are moving from early adoption to mainstream deployment, fundamentally changing how B2B companies sell.

According to a recent McKinsey survey, 67% of B2B companies now use at least one AI-powered sales tool, up from 38% in 2024. The market for these tools — which includes companies like Gong, SignalFox, Clari, and others — is expected to exceed $5 billion by 2028.

The evolution is happening in three waves. The first wave, exemplified by Gong, focused on recording and analyzing sales conversations to provide post-call coaching and deal intelligence. The second wave, represented by companies like Clari, used AI to improve revenue forecasting and pipeline management. The third wave — now emerging — provides real-time AI assistance during live sales interactions.

"The shift from post-hoc analysis to real-time assistance mirrors what we're seeing across enterprise software," said Priya Sharma, a partner at McKinsey's technology practice. "GitHub Copilot transformed development. AI copilots are now transforming sales, customer success, and other customer-facing functions."

Companies in this third wave, including New York-based SignalFox, are reporting significant improvements in sales performance. SignalFox CEO Amira Hassan claims her customers see 15-20% improvement in win rates when using real-time coaching features.

Critics warn that real-time AI coaching could make sales interactions feel less authentic. "There's a fine line between AI-assisted selling and AI-scripted selling," cautioned Mark Roberge, former CRO of HubSpot. "Buyers can tell when a rep is reading from a script, whether that script is written by a manager or an AI."

Hassan disagrees: "Our coaching doesn't script conversations — it surfaces relevant information. The rep still has to be authentic and build relationships. We just make sure they have the right information at the right time."

As the market matures, consolidation is likely. Gong's recent $250 million fundraise signals its intent to build a comprehensive AI platform for revenue teams. ZoomInfo's integration of Chorus across its platform represents the bundling strategy. And startups like SignalFox are betting that purpose-built real-time coaching can carve out a defensible niche.

title: Gong Raises $250M Series E, Valued at $7.5B, Plans Enterprise AI Platform
author: Ingrid Lunden
content:
Gong Raises $250M Series E, Valued at $7.5B, Plans Enterprise AI Platform
By Ingrid Lunden | TechCrunch | January 15, 2026

Gong, the revenue intelligence platform that has become the dominant player in conversational intelligence for sales teams, has raised $250 million in Series E funding at a $7.5 billion valuation. The round was led by Franklin Templeton's venture arm with participation from existing investors including Sequoia Capital, Coatue, and Salesforce Ventures.

Gong co-founder and CEO Amit Bendov said the funding will be used to transform Gong from a conversational intelligence tool into a comprehensive AI platform for enterprise revenue teams. The company plans to expand beyond call recording and analysis into deal management, forecasting, coaching, and — notably — real-time conversation assistance.

"We've built the largest dataset of B2B sales conversations in the world — over 4 billion interactions analyzed," Bendov said. "That data advantage allows us to build AI capabilities that no competitor can match. Real-time coaching, predictive deal scoring, automated follow-ups — these are all coming in 2026."

The mention of real-time coaching is significant. Startups like SignalFox have been gaining traction with real-time conversation coaching features that Gong currently lacks. Gong's platform processes calls after they end, providing insights and coaching recommendations for future conversations. The move to real-time would put Gong in direct competition with this emerging category.

Gong says it now has over 4,000 enterprise customers and surpassed $300 million in ARR in 2025. The company's net revenue retention exceeds 120%, though this is below some newer competitors who benefit from usage-based pricing models.

The Series E comes as the conversational intelligence market continues to consolidate. ZoomInfo's integration of Chorus, Clari's acquisition of Wingman, and Gong's platform expansion are all reducing the number of standalone players. For smaller competitors, the message is clear: scale or be absorbed.

title: ZoomInfo Integrates Chorus AI Capabilities Across Full Revenue Platform
content:
ZoomInfo Integrates Chorus AI Capabilities Across Full Revenue Platform
Business Wire | March 12, 2026

VANCOUVER, WA — ZoomInfo Technologies (NASDAQ: ZI) today announced the full integration of Chorus conversational intelligence capabilities across its revenue platform, completing a multi-year effort to embed AI-powered conversation analysis into every stage of the B2B sales workflow.

The integration means ZoomInfo customers can now access conversation recording, transcription, analysis, and coaching insights alongside ZoomInfo's core contact database and intent data — all within a single platform. New features include AI-generated call summaries that automatically sync to CRM records, conversation-based intent signals that enhance ZoomInfo's buyer intent data, and deal risk scoring based on conversation patterns.

"B2B sales teams don't need more point solutions — they need an integrated platform that connects data, conversations, and actions," said ZoomInfo CEO Henry Schuck. "With Chorus fully integrated, we're the only platform that connects who to call, what to say, and what happened on the call."

ZoomInfo acquired Chorus for $575 million in 2021, betting that conversational intelligence would become essential to its revenue intelligence platform. The integration has taken longer than initially planned, with some Chorus customers noting a period of slower feature development during the transition.

The bundling strategy presents both opportunities and challenges. For ZoomInfo customers already paying for the platform, adding conversation intelligence at marginal cost is attractive. But standalone conversational intelligence providers like Gong argue that bundled solutions sacrifice depth for breadth.

Industry analysts noted that ZoomInfo's approach may pressure smaller conversational intelligence startups that compete on feature parity with Gong. However, companies offering differentiated capabilities — such as SignalFox's real-time coaching or specialized vertical solutions — may be less affected.

"The bundling play works for companies buying 'good enough' conversational intelligence," said Forrester analyst Seth Marrs. "But for sales teams that view conversation intelligence as a strategic advantage, purpose-built tools will continue to win."
